channel.title: Jane Rehearsal — Portfolio
channel.description: Distributed-systems engineer, technology essayist, and conference speaker.

item.title: The 2010 BlackBerry Outage Was Not About BlackBerry
item.description: Three days in October 2011 when the world's most secure messaging platform went silent — and what an obscure SAN failure has to teach us about modern multi-region replication.

item.title: The Quiet Cost of Legible Systems
item.description: On how observability turns engineering trade-offs into political ones, and what to do about it.

item.title: Knight Capital, Twelve Years On
item.description: A re-reading of the 45-minute trading-floor meltdown that erased a company, with new attention to the deployment script that did it.

item.title: The S3 Console Day
item.description: Why the 2017 S3 outage made us all rethink "static" status pages.

item.title: A Brief History of the Phrase "Cattle, Not Pets"
item.description: A short etymology of the most-quoted phrase in modern infrastructure, with a defense of pets.

item.title: Postmortems Are an Editing Problem
item.description: How to get an honest postmortem out of a reluctant team — borrow from the rules of essay editing.

item.title: A Survey of Anti-Entropy Mechanisms in Production Systems
item.description: A practitioner-oriented survey of anti-entropy techniques (Merkle trees, gossip, hinted handoff) used in production deployments of the largest distributed databases of the past decade.

item.title: Probabilistic Model Checking of Eventually-Consistent Stores
item.description: We show that the verification of bounded staleness in a class of eventually-consistent stores reduces to a probabilistic model checking problem with polynomial-time decidability.
